title: Ramsey Theory for Hypergraphs
description: Extends Ramsey's theorem from graphs (k=2) to k-uniform hypergraphs. The hypergraph Ramsey theorem states that for any k, r, n, sufficiently large sets have monochromatic k-subsets under any r-coloring.

overview.historicalContext: Ramsey (1930) proved the theorem in full generality for k-element subsets, not just edges. The k=2 (graph) case became most famous. Erdős and Rado (1952) showed hypergraph Ramsey numbers grow as towers of exponentials with height proportional to k.
overview.problemStatement:
How does Ramsey theory extend to hypergraphs and higher dimensions?

**Answer**: The hypergraph Ramsey theorem states that for k-uniform hypergraphs with r colors, sufficiently large sets contain monochromatic k-subsets. The Ramsey numbers grow as iterated towers.
overview.text: Ramsey theory extends to hypergraphs via the k-uniform Ramsey theorem.
overview.proofStrategy: Define k-subsets, colorings, and the Ramsey property. Show k=1 is pigeonhole, k=2 is classical Ramsey. Axiomatize the general existence. Define tower function for growth rates.
keyInsights: k=1 is pigeonhole, k=2 is classical graph Ramsey, k>=3 is hypergraph Ramsey
Growth rate: k-uniform Ramsey numbers grow as height-k towers of 2
The stepping-up lemma converts (k-1)-uniform bounds to k-uniform bounds
